texts.text: 14 Evening Prayer for the New Year 14

commandments of the Lord and fulfil them. And do not follow your heart and your eyes after which you go astray. Thus may you remember and fulfil all my commandments and be holy unto your God. I am the Lord your God who led you out of the land of Egypt in order to be your God. I am the Lord your God.

All this is truth and faithfulness and it is established unto us that He, the Lord, is our God and there is none beside Him and we are Israel, His people. It is He who frees us from the hand of kings, our King who redeems us from the palm of all oppressors. It is God who requites our enemies on our behalf and pays retribution to all pursuers of our soul. It is He who performs unfathomable deeds of grandeur, wonders without number. He who sets our soul in the course of life and does not allow our feet to falter. He who leads us over the heights of our adversaries and raises our condition above all who hate us. It is He who effects wonders for us and revenge on Pharaoh, signs and miracles in the land of the sons of Ham, who slays all the first-born of Egypt in His wrath and leads His people Israel from their midst to eternal freedom. It is He who causes His children to pass between the divisions of the Red Sea, their persecutors and their enemies did He drown in the depths. His children saw His strength, they praised and acknowledged His Name, they willingly accepted His dominion over them. Moses and the children of Israel answered in song to Thee with great rejoicing and they all said:
Who is like Thee among the mighty, O Lord? Who is like Thee, glorious in holiness, awe-inspiring in fame, worker of wonder?
Thy children saw Thy kingdom when Thou didst divide the sea before Moses: this is my God, they answered and said: The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.
And it is said: For the Lord has freed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who has redeemed Israel.

uncertainties: Paragraph 1 begins mid-sentence ('commandments of the Lord...'). Nothing on this page comes before it.
'worker of wonder?' is printed in the singular, 'wonder', and ends with a question mark.
The cues are unpointed Hebrew with no vowel marks.

enlarged_readings.text: Right column role label: 'פֿאָרבעטער:' (Forbeter). Left column role label: 'געמיינדע:' (Gemeinde, the congregation). Combined abbreviation, set small under the end of the line ברכו את־יי המברך: 'קו״ח'. Language/script: the labels are Yiddish (German-derived words) in Hebrew square script. Vowel points: the right label has a rafe over פ and a kamats under the first letter after it, which reads as אָ. The left label has no vowel points I can see.
uncertainties: In the right label, the letter carrying the kamats looks a bit like ח in this print. I read it as אָ. As printed it could look like 'פֿחָרבעטער'.
Abbreviation read as ק, ו, gershayim, ח. I have not expanded it.
The left label's spacing before the colon looks like 'געמיינדע :'. I can't tell whether the space is intentional.

enlarged_readings.text: יש לצרף אלהיכם לאמת, אכן יתן רוח מעט שלא יבולע הא׳.
uncertainties: The instruction is in Rashi script. I transliterated it letter by letter into square script.
I read 'אכן' from Rashi א+כ+ן. The א is the shape most open to doubt.
I read 'שלא' from glyphs that look like ס/ט+ל+ח, which are the Rashi forms of ש, ל, א.
'יבולע': the ו is small and could be absent ('יבלע').
Final 'הא׳' is printed as an abbreviation with a geresh. I have not expanded it.
The comma after 'לאמת' and the final period both appear in print.

enlarged_readings.text: Congregation response: 'Blessed is the Lord who is called blessed for ever and ever.' There is no punctuation after the first 'ever'. A period follows the second 'ever', which runs over to the next line.
uncertainties: There is a small mark below the 'l' of 'called', which looks like a speck in the print and not punctuation. It is not next to 'ever'.

limits: I read only s23 and the three crops. I did not consult any transcription, OCR, XML or other edition.
The s22 crop shows only the end of the verse plus the Rashi instruction. There is no wider context, so I did not interpret the instruction's wording against customary practice.
